content.comment_body: Hello! I have set up communication between a [product_name] and a [version_no] following a guide for client configuration found on the [company_name] website. My question is how to set up communication with [product_name] as a server instead. I want to control communication from the [version_no]. I see the option to add a server connection in 'TOOLS->ETHERNET CONNECTION', but how do I do this in [product_name_software]? Also, which data is accessible in [product_name]? Is it the data I define in VM Mapping and network inputs/outputs, etc.? Best regards, [user_name]
Is there a specific reason you want the [version_no] to act as a client? I am not sure I understand the motivation for this setup.

One reason is curiosity—I would like to know how since it's available. Additionally, it seems logical for the [version_no] to be the client/master with the [product_name] units as servers/slaves. The main reason is for a project where my customer wants to use 700 [product_name] units and one [version_no] to gather their statuses and send setpoints. (There's also a possibility of using a [version_no] since the [version_no] might be too small.) I'm still figuring out the best method, but by making the [version_no] the client that polls each [product_name], I may be able to loop through the communications rather than establishing 700 simultaneous connections. The process is not time-critical. Any alternative suggestions are welcome. Regards, [user_name]
Please refer to the attached video for further information.
Thank you for the video. How do I implement this in the [version_no]?
Perhaps this link will be helpful: [url]

I've reviewed that document, and based on what I've read, I believe my [version_no] has to be set as the client and the [product_name] as the client too. This way, I can manage all connections from the [version_no] without too many simultaneous connections. However, I have not found an example demonstrating how to configure the [product_name] as a server that responds to requests from the [version_no]. If you know of any such examples, please share. Best regards, [user_name]

Compared to the [product_name] communication guide, you'll need to make these changes: To have the [version_no] as the client, enable the 'Establish active connection' option (refer to page 2). Select the server connection rather than the client connection on page 5.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are investigating ways to configure communication between a large number of [product_name] units and a [version_no], specifically with [product_name] as the server and [version_no] as the client. While existing documentation and guides from [company_name] mostly cover client setups for [product_name], users require step-by-step instructions for server configuration within [product_name_software]. There is uncertainty around which data points on the [product_name] can be accessed by the [version_no] and how to efficiently handle many simultaneous connections. Users seek practical guidance and working examples for implementing this architecture.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want clear and practical instructions for configuring [product_name] as a server and allowing polling/control from the [version_no]. They also want clarification on what data within [product_name] is accessible and how to manage multiple device connections efficiently.
